summary: Bug-fix verification for slow 'L' gesture detection (PLENA SNAP login gate). (1) Wrote a node unit test that EXTRACTS the real dist/isLSign source from LoginGate.jsx (no copy-paste) and runs 7 synthetic 21-landmark fixtures: clean L, tilted-18deg lazy L with moderately extended thumb (the reported bug case), fist, open palm, index-only-with-folded-thumb, empty input. All 7 behave as expected. (2) Built a 'legacy threshold' variant of the same function (0.8*scale thumbExt, cos<0.7, 1.15 folds, lm[6].y index check) and proved the lazy/tilted L is REJECTED by the old geometry but ACCEPTED by the new one -> the relaxation demonstrably fixes the latency complaint (diag: thumb ratio 0.618 vs old >0.8 needed; index/thumb angle 40deg, cos 0.766 vs old cos<0.7 needed). (3) Verified constants in source: HOLD_MS===550, decay dt*0.5, all three GestureRecognizer confidences 0.3, three 1.25 fold multipliers, cos<0.85, thumbExt 0.55*scale. (4) Frontend smoke on public URL: gate loads, LOGIN -> scanning stage with eyes + progress bar (0%) and Turkish hint renders, MediaPipe GestureRecognizer initialized with the new options with NO invalid-option warnings (only benign 'Created TensorFlow Lite XNNPACK delegate for CPU' info log), PIN 574913 unlocks to attract screen. (5) Backend regression: 4/4 passed in test_login_gate.py subset - verify-gesture with /app/assets/l_sign_test.jpg -> ok:true (exactly 1 Gemini VLM call, budget respected), verify-pin 574913 -> 200 {ok:true}, no-header/wrong-pin -> 401. Zero caricature generations.

issues: In the scanning screenshot the left eye renders fully but the right eye appears as a thin horizontal line - most likely a mid-blink frame of EyeTracking (blinkInterval 4200ms) captured by the screenshot, but if blinks are not synchronised across eyes it looks like a rendering glitch. Low priority, visual only.

critical_code_review_comments: isLSign relaxation is safe against the tested negative fixtures (fist / open palm / index-only), so no false-positive regression was observed; however the angle gate is now cos<0.85 (~32deg) and a very narrow 'index up + thumb slightly splayed' pose could pass - if false unlocks appear in the field, tighten to ~0.8 rather than reverting the thumbExt change (thumbExt was the dominant blocker in the bug case).

verifyFrame() resets heldRef to 0 on VLM rejection; after the HOLD_MS reduction to 550ms this makes a rejected attempt feel like a full restart. Consider resetting to ~50% so a genuine L re-confirms faster (optional UX polish).
loop() useCallback dependency list is [succeed] but loop does not use succeed; harmless but misleading - deps should be empty or include verifyRef only.

rca_of_the_issue: Original slow detection was caused by two over-strict gates in isLSign: thumbExt required the thumb tip to be >0.8*palm-scale from the index MCP and the index/thumb angle required cos<0.7 (>45deg). A natural, slightly tilted L with a moderately splayed thumb measures ~0.62*scale and ~40deg (cos 0.766) and therefore failed both gates, so progress only accumulated in rare frames while the old dt*1.5 decay erased it between them. Relaxing to 0.55*scale / cos<0.85, halving decay to dt*0.5, lowering HOLD_MS to 550ms and dropping MediaPipe confidences to 0.3 makes that pose pass continuously. Verified by differential unit test (old=false, new=true on the identical fixture).
